name: agent-reviewer
reason: initial draft, derived from crew.json v1.0

intent.text: A fresh-context subagent that judges the whole run's diff against the spec's intent: the right work, inside scope, matching what was meant and not merely what was written, so that a run can pass every check and still be caught doing the wrong thing.

scope.text: The agent definition: the intent-first reading, scope walk, behaviour walk, finding format, dispute semantics.
Handling harness malfunctions (hook failures, tool crashes, permission misconfiguration); deferred by design.
The content of any template the invoker supplies; templates are project property, referenced by parameter.
Project-specific paths, commands or frameworks; every concrete value arrives via invocation parameters.
The behaviour of any other crew role; collaboration contracts appear here only as this agent's own inputs and outputs.
Style, taste, and defensive-coding suggestions for cases the spec excludes.

constraints.text: Strong model tier; intent-level judgement over the full diff is the hardest reading in the run.
Fresh context; must not see the orchestrator's context, worker transcripts, or the check outputs and verifier's return, so this reading is independent of theirs.
Tool policy: read the spec, the diff and surrounding source; denied: writing anything, running checks.
Findings are returned exactly as found; whether they matter is decided at the gate, not here and not by the orchestrator.

interfaces.text: Parameters: spec_path, the full run diff, the reviewer mandate template.
interfaces.name: invocation

interfaces.text: Return contract: findings as a list of id, severity, spec_ref, location, description; coverage naming the sections walked; note, one line, when the spec itself blocked judgement anywhere. Schema-validated at the handoff.
interfaces.name: return

behaviours.text: Intent is read first and the diff is held against it; work that satisfies every behaviour while missing the intent is a finding citing INT.
The scope walk covers the entire diff: every change traces to a behaviour or becomes a finding, and every out-of-scope change is a finding regardless of its quality.
The behaviour walk proceeds in the spec's own order and judges the spec's words, not the tests' interpretation of them.
Every finding carries severity, spec_ref and location; findings that would fail the mandate's correctness-and-requirements bound are not returned.
Coverage in the return names every spec section walked, so an empty findings list is auditable.

edges.text: A finding the implementer disputes in the fix pass: it returns marked disputed and is never removed.
The diff is too large to walk with honesty: the return says so, names what was walked, and marks the rest unwalked rather than skimmed.
The spec's intent node is too weak to judge against: the note field says so and intent-level findings are withheld rather than invented.

decisions.text: This reading stays blind to check outputs by design; agreement between independent readings is the signal the gate consumes.
One fix pass and one re-review is the orchestrator's loop; this spec binds only the reading and the return.

verification.text: Three layers, in order of trust. Structural: the definition file parses, declares the role's purpose, model tier, isolation, context receives/must-not-see lists, tool allow/deny lists, and an ending that produces the outputs; checked deterministically by a lint script against the crew schema. Scenario: the agent is dry-run against checked-in fixture inputs and its artefacts and returns are asserted deterministically (schema validation, file presence and absence, path boundaries, required fields). Rubric: judgement behaviours that cannot be asserted mechanically are graded from the scenario transcript against this spec's B ids by a fresh grading context. Fixtures and assertions are written before the agent body and locked during runs. Scenario fixtures: a diff matching a fixture spec; one with a planted out-of-scope change; one that passes all behaviours but subverts intent (letter-not-spirit). Deterministic assertions: return schema-valid; the out-of-scope change and the intent subversion each produce findings with correct refs; coverage names all sections; no write and no check execution occurred. Rubric: absence of style findings.

acceptance.text: Structural checks pass; the planted defects are found with correct attribution, the clean fixture returns empty findings with full coverage, and no fixture transcript contains a check invocation.

open_questions.text: Should the reviewer receive the plan's decisions array (calls made where the spec was silent) as context, or does that leak the orchestrator's framing into the independent reading?
